thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — possible cross-tenant routing/KV cache anomaly in dedicated pool dp-us-east-3. Symptoms: unexpected KV hits from tenant Calyx-Tx referencing keys from pool 'shared-legacy'. Pager sent to @Dana. Investigate routing, recent deploys, and audit logs. https://internal.incidents/2056789123

Dana: I'm taking this. Paging infra/SRE. @Sanjay @Eli can you join? I'll start customer comms hold message for Calyx-Tx (CS contact: Amy).

Sanjay: on call. Starting with route table and prefix mappings for dp-us-east-3. Running quick checks now.

Eli: looking at runtime telemetry — seeing a small spike in cross-tenant KV hits between 02:11-02:18 UTC, correlates with a deploy to dp-us-east-3 ~02:10.

DeployBot: rollout: service/router-svc v12.3.7 -> dp-us-east-3 by ci/devops (commit 9f7c1a4) at 2024-11-05T02:09:34Z.

Sanjay: found a suspicious /16 entry that was mistakenly added to the global routing table for the dedicated pool. Extract: 
```
# ip route show table dp-us-east-3
10.4.0.0/16 dev eth0 proto static scope link pref 100 pool_id=calyx-tx
10.5.0.0/16 dev eth1 proto static scope link pref 100 pool_id=shared-legacy  <-- ambiguous
10.5.0.0/16 dev eth2 proto static scope link pref 90 pool_id=dp-default
```
That duplicate /16 for 10.5.0.0/16 looks like the root cause — overlap allowed some keys to be routed to the wrong pool.

Raj: security note — until we confirm, treat this as potential cross-tenant read exposure. Which keys were affected? Any PII in the sampled keys?

Eli: sample of impacted keys (sanitized): calyx:session:xyz, shared-legacy:feature:abc. From logs we see ~120 accesses where pool_id from auth header != pool_id resolved by router. Most access patterns look like token-scoped operations, not bulk dumps.

Amy: contacting Calyx-Tx support lead to say we detected an issue, mitigation in progress, and we'll share impact summary ASAP. Draft: "We're investigating a routing misconfiguration that may have caused limited KV access cross-tenant. No confirmed PII access; we'll update soon." Want approval before send.

Dana: approved. Send the hold message now. Marking customer impact = potential, limited scope. No public post yet.

Sanjay: mitigation step 1: remove ambiguous route and apply strict prefix binding. Executing now: 
```
# remove bad route
ip route delete 10.5.0.0/16 table dp-us-east-3 dev eth1
# enforce strict-prefix policy
redwood-routes apply --pool dp-us-east-3 --policy strict-prefix-enforce
```

Sanjay: done. Route removed and policy applied. Pushing a config check to ensure no /16 overlaps remain.

Eli: telemetry — immediate drop in cross-pool KV resolution. Before: 12.3% of Calyx requests resolved to shared-legacy; after: 0.2% and those are retries/in-flight. Latency normal.

Raj: pulling audit logs for data access. Running grep across kv-access logs for the window 02:08-02:20 UTC.

Raj: quick summary from audit: 118 misrouted accesses; keys touched were mostly feature flags and session tokens. No records matching our PII detectors (ssn, name, email) in that time window. Exporting logs to secure bucket for deeper review.

Amy: messaging update to Calyx-Tx: "Mitigation applied, we found limited misrouting affecting ~120 requests. We have no evidence of PII exposure. We're performing a full audit and will share the findings by EOD." Sending now.

Kate: can we pin this to the recent router-svc v12.3.7 deploy? If yes we should consider a rollback or hotfix to the route validation logic in the control plane.

Sanjay: the change that introduced the ambiguous route was a control-plane regression in route-merge logic (PR #412). I'm isolating the patch and reverting the offending merge on the control plane. Hotfix PR in progress.

DeployBot: rollback requested: control-plane-prog revert PR#412 -> staging. (manual approval required).

Dana: handing off to SRE/infra for post-incident follow-up and RCA. I'll keep this thread open for timeline notes. SRE, please own the follow-up ticket and notify compliance (Raj) when the full audit is complete.

Sanjay: creating INC ticket INC-2056789123 with actions: (1) revert PR#412, (2) add route overlap unit tests, (3) extend KV audit window, (4) customer notification timeline.

Raj: I'll continue the log forensics and record evidence. No escalation to legal required at this point, but I'll flag if anything changes.

Eli: runtime checklist: backfill metrics for the last 7 days to check for prior noisy neighbors; adding alert to detect >0.5% cross-pool KV resolution rate.

Amy: Calyx replied: thanks, please send me the full report when ready. They appreciated the quick mitigation.

Dana: summary for ticket: Impact: Calyx-Tx experienced ~120 misrouted KV accesses due to a route-merge bug in control plane after deploy. Mitigation: removed ambiguous route, enforced strict-prefix policy, reverted merge. Customer notified. Next steps: RCA, tests, two-week follow-up with Calyx, postmortem.

IncidentBot: incident INC-2056789123 created and assigned to SRE. Slack thread archived for timeline capture.

Sanjay: leaving notes in infra/ticket/INC-2056789123. Handing off to oncall rotation for tomorrow.

Dana: thanks team — closing pager. If anything new appears, reopen here. :thumbsup:
